prompt_text: Who is the best moving company in Pleasanton CA for a local move?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but “best” depends on your needs (size of move, date, budget, whether you need packing/storage, stairs, fragile/valuables). A quick plan:

1) Quick questions so I can recommend specific companies
- Exact Pleasanton zip (or cross-town move)?
- Move date or window?
- Size: studio, 1BR, 3BR, etc. and any large/fragile items (piano, safe)?
- Do you need packing, storage, disassembly/reassembly?
Answer those and I’ll tailor suggestions.

2) Short list to start your search
If you want quick names to call, consider getting estimates from 3–4 of:
- Local Tri‑Valley/ East Bay mover (search “Pleasanton movers” on Google or Yelp for highly rated local teams)
- Two Men and a Truck (has Bay Area/ Tri‑Valley locations)
- Bellhop (app-based, same-day/local moves in many metro areas)
- College HUNKS Hauling Junk & Moving (national brand active in the Bay Area)

(Notes: I can’t browse right now to pull current local ratings; those are commonly available options in the Bay Area. I recommend also checking top local results on Yelp/Google for small, highly rated independent companies — they often get the best local service.)

3) How to pick the best one (checklist)
- Get at least 3 in‑home (or video) estimates — avoid large binding estimates based only on inventory lists.
- Ask whether the estimate is binding, non‑binding, or guaranteed not-to-exceed.
- Verify insurance and ask about valuation coverage (released value vs. full replacement).
- Confirm license/registration (ask for company registration or USDOT number for interstate moves).
- Ask about extra fees: stairs, long carry, elevator, shuttle truck, bulky items, packing materials.
- Read recent Google/Yelp reviews, specifically for local moves and any complaints about damage or hidden fees.
- Ask about crew experience, truck size, COVID/cleaning policies if relevant, and cancellation policy.
- Get everything in writing (date, time window, estimated hours or flat price, included services, payment terms).

4) Sample questions to ask a mover
- “Is this estimate binding? If not, how could cost change?”
- “What is your hourly rate, minimum hours, truck size, and crew size?”
- “Do you charge extra for stairs, long carries, or bulky items?”
- “What insurance/valuation do you provide? Can I buy higher coverage?”
- “Do you provide packing materials and packing services? Cost?”
- “What is your cancellation/rescheduling policy?”

If you tell me your zip, move size, and date I’ll:
- suggest a short list of highly rated local companies to call,
- draft a message you can send to movers to request estimates,
- or create a comparison table to help you choose. Which would you like?
